title: U.S. House · Washington's 9th District
area: South Seattle, Renton, Kent, Auburn, and parts of Tacoma in the South Sound.

context.text: Washington uses a top-two primary open to all voters regardless of party. Incumbent D. Adam Smith and Douglas Michael Basler advanced from the August 4, 2026 primary, defeating Kshama Sawant (Independent Party of Washington), Melissa Chaudhry (D), and Jacob Perasso (Socialist Workers Party). Smith won the primary with 50.2% of the vote.

candidates.name: D. Adam Smith
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 1997); Ranking Member, House Armed Services Committee

summary.text: D. Adam Smith is the Democratic incumbent for Washington's 9th Congressional District. A lawyer and former Seattle city prosecutor, he was elected to the Washington State Senate at age 25 and to Congress in 1996, taking office in 1997. He is the Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee and chaired the committee in the 116th and 117th Congresses.

background.text: Born June 15, 1965, in Washington, D.C., and raised in SeaTac, Washington; graduated from Tyee High School in 1983.
Attended Western Washington University for a year, then graduated from Fordham University in 1987 with a degree in political science; earned a law degree from the University of Washington in 1990.

Worked as a lawyer at Cromwell, Mendoza and Belur beginning in 1992 and as a prosecutor for the City of Seattle from 1993 to 1995, focusing on drunk driving and domestic violence cases, according to his official biography.

Won election to the Washington State Senate in 1990 from the 33rd Legislative District, defeating a 16-year incumbent; his official biography says he was 25 when he took office in January 1991. Re-elected in 1994; served on the Education and Law and Justice Committees and chaired the Law and Justice Committee.
Elected to the U.S. House in 1996 and assumed office in January 1997.

Has served on the House Armed Services Committee since entering Congress; previously chaired its Air and Land Forces subcommittee and its Terrorism, Unconventional Threats and Capabilities subcommittee, and also served on the Foreign Affairs and Intelligence Committees.
Chaired the full Armed Services Committee in the 116th and 117th Congresses (2019-2022) and is its Ranking Member in the 119th Congress.
Co-founded the bipartisan Congressional Caucus for Effective Foreign Assistance; a 2020 news report also lists him as a member of the Council on Foreign Relations.
According to his official biography, married Sara Bickle-Eldridge in 1993; they have two children.

priorities.text: Says he is focused on lowering rent and building more housing, standing up to the Trump administration on democracy and social-safety-net issues, and putting people before corporate profits.
Says his approach is to listen to constituents, set realistic goals, and deliver practical solutions rather than pursue an ideological agenda.
priorities.quote: Listen to communities and constituents, set ambitious but realistic goals and expectations, and deliver practical solutions that make life better for everyone in work for people in Washington's Ninth District.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he sponsored a zoning and permitting reform bill to incentivize cities and counties to cut red tape and build more housing near jobs and transit.
positions.quote: He sponsored a major zoning and permitting reform bill to incentivize cities and counties to cut red tape and build more housing near jobs and transit.

positions.summary: Cosponsored legislation to block cuts to Medicaid and SNAP and supported protecting Washington's health-care model, including the State-Based Universal Health Care Act.
positions.quote: He co-sponsored the Hands Off Medicaid and SNAP Act to block GOP efforts to slash health care and food assistance for seniors, veterans, and working families.

positions.summary: Cosponsored the Ensuring Women's Right to Reproductive Freedom Act opposing efforts to criminalize interstate travel for abortion.
positions.quote: He is a co-sponsor of the Ensuring Women's Right to Reproductive Freedom Act, pushing back on MAGA-backed attempts to criminalize interstate travel for abortion.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he is introducing a bill to create a minimum tax rate on large corporations.
positions.quote: create a minimum tax rate on massive corporations so they finally pay their fair share

positions.summary: Signed an amicus brief supporting a lawsuit against the Trump administration's use of emergency powers to impose broad tariffs, arguing Congress holds exclusive authority to regulate tariffs and commerce.
positions.quote: Adam signed onto an amicus brief that continues to affirm Congress's Article I exclusive legislative power to impose tariffs and regulate commerce and support a lawsuit brought by 12 States' Attorneys against the Trump Administration for abusing emergency powers under IEEPA to unlawfully impose reckless, across-the-board tariffs.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he supports raising the federal minimum wage to $20 an hour.
positions.quote: he supports raising the federal minimum wage to $20/hour

positions.summary: Campaign site says he is leading an effort to transition the economy to clean energy and take on large polluters.
positions.quote: He is leading the effort to transition our economy to a clean-energy future by reducing our dependence on foreign energy, creating green jobs and taking on Big Polluters.

record.text: Sponsored the End Hedge Fund Control of American Homes Act to require corporate landlords to divest single-family homes.
Sponsored the Promoting Affordable Housing Near Transit Act, cutting red tape for transit agencies to develop housing near light rail stations.
As Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee, brokered a bipartisan and bicameral investigation into Department of Defense military operations in the Caribbean.
Cosponsored multiple War Powers Resolutions directing the removal of U.S. armed forces from Venezuela.
Cosponsored the VISIBLE Act, requiring immigration enforcement officers to display visible identification during public-facing enforcement actions.

summary.text: Douglas Michael Basler (known as Doug Basler) is the Republican nominee for Washington's 9th Congressional District. A Spokane native who has worked in marketing and as a volunteer youth pastor, corporate trainer and musician, he has run for the seat before and advanced from the August 2026 top-two primary with 24.1% of the vote.

background.text: Born in Spokane, Washington; Ballotpedia lists his career experience as marketing and work as a volunteer youth pastor, corporate trainer and musician, with affiliations including Street Church USA, the Salvation Army, Street Feed and the Rescue Mission.

A 2020 Mercer Island Reporter profile described him as a former senior vice chairman of the King County Republican Party, president and founder of EZTVSpots.com, a graduate of Multnomah University, and a volunteer church youth leader for more than 30 years.

Previously ran against Smith for the 9th District seat; Ballotpedia lists him on the general-election ballot in 2014, 2016, 2020 and 2022, and KIRO 7 reported in 2022 that he had lost to Smith by wide margins each time.
Ran for King County Elections Director in 2023, receiving 15.9% of the vote against incumbent Julie Wise.

priorities.text: Describes a platform he calls the Opportunity Revolution: protecting freedom, rewarding work, removing unnecessary barriers, keeping communities safe and giving people the opportunity to build a good life.
priorities.quote: Government can’t promise you a great life, but it can and should protect your freedom, reward work, remove unnecessary barriers, keep communities safe and give people the opportunity to build one

priorities.text: His campaign website lists affordability, family, safety, opportunity and a better future for children as his focus.
priorities.quote: My focus is simple: affordability, family, safety, opportunity, and a better future for our children.

statements.quote: making housing more attainable by reducing unnecessary barriers to building
statements.context: In a statement to the Renton Reporter (Oct. 2, 2026)

statements.quote: I’m pro-life and hope people choose life, but I do not support a federal abortion ban. I strongly support IVF and contraception, and I believe we should do much more for children and families, especially children at risk.
statements.context: In a statement to the Renton Reporter (Oct. 2, 2026)

statements.quote: I also urge a YES vote on all three statewide initiatives: IL26-001 for parents’ rights, IL26-638 to protect girls’ sports and safe spaces, and IP26-645 to repeal Washington’s new income tax.
statements.context: In a statement to the Renton Reporter (Oct. 2, 2026)

researchNotes: Douglas (Doug) Basler's statements come from a Renton Reporter candidate statement (Oct. 2, 2026) and a campaign-website line quoted by MyNorthwest; his campaign website itself was not located. Smith's federal key votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Douglas Michael Basler has a Ballotpedia page (listed under Doug Basler) with a short biography; no campaign website was found, and his biography draws on Ballotpedia and 2020 and 2022 news coverage.
